newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Telesis CEO sees SBC merger in Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Telesis CEO sees SBC merger in Q1 '97.

text.p: Pacific Telesis Group chief executive officer Philip Quigley believes prospects for completing Pac Tel's planned merger with SBC Communications Inc are good, despite complaints from long distance carriers and others and a closing will likely be in 1997's first quarter.

"I think the prospects for this merger happening are good and I think it will take to the first quarter of next year to do it," Quigley said, speaking to the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference.
Pacific Telesis and SBC Corp agreed to a $16.7 billion merger in April, a combination that would create the second or third largest telecommunications company in the United States.
Long distance carriers have complained to Congress that the merger, and one planned by Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp, would pose anti-trust issues giving the Bell combinations unfair advantages.

Meanwhile, consumer groups in California have complained to the California Public Utilities Commission that a merger would not be in the best interest of consumers. The CPUC as well as the U.S. Justice Department must approve the merger.
But the merger is planned amid a backdrop of widespread deregulation of the telecommunications market, brought on by the Telecommunications Reform Act of 1996.

Quigley said the Act presents "a seachange in public policy" aimed at bringing competition to the telecommunications industry. However, Pac Tel and other Bell companies have challenged the U.S. Federal Communications Commission's interpretation of the Act as Congress passed it. Quigley believes the FCC has taken out some of the pure market features of the Act in its interpretive rules. He said the challenge should be heard on Thursday in the eighth Circuit Court.
Pacific Telesis is charging ahead with plans to enter new markets.
Its wireless personal communications services business it launched in San Diego last month will be rolled out throughout California and Nevada over the next year, he said.
And Pacific Telesis definitely plans to enter the long distance business he said.
